through indirectly ameliorating the impairment in one-carbon metabolism caused by one of these other nutrients. Deﬁciencies
of other nutrients, including vitamin C and zinc, have also been implicated in NTDs but the evidence is limited and the data
are inconsistent.
Obesity and diabetes
There are other potentially modiﬁable risk factors for NTDs. Women who are obese compared to those of normal body mass index
(BMI) are more likely to have a child affected with an NTD (and indeed other malformations including congenital heart defects).
